Role.name: ASPIRANT
Role.description: Civil Services Aspirant studying for Prelims and Mains

Exam.name: Combined Section Officers' Grade B LDCE
Combined Stenographers' Grade B/Grade I LDCE

SyllabusNode.title: Constitutional Framework & Historical Underpinnings
SyllabusNode.description: Regulating Act 1773 to Independence Act 1947, Constituent Assembly, Preamble, Salient Features, Basic Structure doctrine.

SyllabusNode.title: Fundamental Rights, DPSP & Fundamental Duties
SyllabusNode.description: Articles 12-35 (Writs, Reasonable Restrictions, Exceptions), Directive Principles (Part IV), Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, 42nd & 86th Amendments).

SyllabusNode.title: Union & State Executive
SyllabusNode.description: President (Election, Powers, Pardoning, Veto, Ordinance Art 123), Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, Governor (Art 163, 213, Discretionary powers).

SyllabusNode.title: Union & State Legislature (Parliament & Assemblies)
SyllabusNode.description: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Parliamentary Committees, Budgetary procedure, Motions (No-Confidence, Adjournment), Privileges, Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule).

SyllabusNode.title: Judiciary (Supreme Court, High Courts, Subordinate Courts)
SyllabusNode.description: Jurisdiction (Original, Appellate, Advisory Art 143), Judicial Review, Collegium System, Judicial Activism vs Overreach, Contempt of Court, Fast Track Courts.

SyllabusNode.title: Constitutional & Non-Constitutional Bodies
SyllabusNode.description: Election Commission (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315-323), CAG (Art 148-151), Finance Commission (Art 280), GST Council (Art 279A), NITI Aayog, NHRC, CVC, CBI, Lokpal.

SyllabusNode.title: Local Self-Government (Panchayats & Municipalities)
SyllabusNode.description: 73rd Amendment (11th Schedule, 29 subjects, PESA Act 1996), 74th Amendment (12th Schedule, 18 subjects), State Finance Commission, District Planning Committees.

SyllabusNode.title: National Income Accounting & Economic Growth
SyllabusNode.description: GDP, GNP, NNP, Real vs Nominal GDP, GVA, Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), Green GDP, Inclusive Growth indicators.

SyllabusNode.title: Money, Banking & Monetary Policy
SyllabusNode.description: RBI functions, Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), Repo, Reverse Repo, SDF, CRR, SLR, Inflation Targeting (4% +/- 2%), NBFCs, Bad Banks (NARCL), Digital Rupee (CBDC).

SyllabusNode.title: Fiscal Policy & Public Finance
SyllabusNode.description: Union Budget components (Revenue vs Capital Receipts/Expenditure), Fiscal Deficit, Primary Deficit, FRBM Act, Debt-to-GDP ratio, GST architecture.

SyllabusNode.title: External Sector & Balance of Payments
SyllabusNode.description: Current Account Deficit (CAD), Capital Account Convertibility, Foreign Exchange Reserves, FDI vs FPI, NEER vs REER, Devaluation vs Depreciation, WTO agreements.

SyllabusNode.title: Inflation, Poverty & Employment
SyllabusNode.description: CPI vs WPI, Headline vs Core inflation, Cost-push vs Demand-pull, Multidimensional Poverty Index (NITI Aayog / UNDP), Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).

SyllabusNode.title: Agriculture & Food Processing
SyllabusNode.description: Minimum Support Price (MSP, CACP formula A2+FL vs C2), PM-KISAN, PMFBY, Agri-infrastructure, Buffer stocks, PDS reforms, Direct Seeded Rice, Millets (Shree Anna).

SyllabusNode.title: Geomorphology & Earth Interior
SyllabusNode.description: Plate Tectonics, Continental Drift, Earthquake waves (P & S waves), Shadow zones, Volcanism, Landforms (Fluvial, Aeolian, Glacial, Karst).

SyllabusNode.title: Climatology & Indian Monsoon
SyllabusNode.description: Atmospheric layers, Heat budget, Planetary winds, Jet streams, El Nino, La Nina, Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), Western Disturbances, Tropical vs Temperate Cyclones.

SyllabusNode.title: Oceanography & Marine Resources
SyllabusNode.description: Ocean floor relief, Ocean currents (Warm vs Cold), Salinity distribution, Tides, Marine pollution, Coral reefs bleaching, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

SyllabusNode.title: Physical Geography of India
SyllabusNode.description: Himalayan mountain system (Passes, Valleys, Glaciers), Indo-Gangetic Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Coastal plains, Island territories, Soil types of India (ICAR 8 groups).

SyllabusNode.title: Indian River Systems & Water Resources
SyllabusNode.description: Himalayan drainage (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra systems) vs Peninsular drainage (Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Narmada, Tapti), Interlinking of rivers, Groundwater depletion.

SyllabusNode.title: Ecology Fundamentals & Ecosystems
SyllabusNode.description: Levels of organization, Biomes, Food chains/webs, Ecological Pyramids (Energy, Biomass, Numbers), Bioaccumulation vs Biomagnification, Ecotone & Edge Effect.

SyllabusNode.title: Biodiversity & Conservation (Protected Areas)
SyllabusNode.description: In-situ vs Ex-situ, National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves (MAB program), Tiger Reserves (NTCA, Project Tiger), Elephant Reserves, Ramsar Wetlands.

SyllabusNode.title: Climate Change & Global Warming
SyllabusNode.description: Greenhouse gases (GWP, Radiative forcing), Ocean acidification, IPCC Assessment Reports (AR6), UNFCCC COP summits (Kyoto, Paris Agreement, COP28 UAE Consensus).

SyllabusNode.title: Environmental Conventions & Legislation
SyllabusNode.description: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (2022 Amendment, CITES schedules), Environment Protection Act 1986, Forest Conservation Act 1980, Biological Diversity Act 2002, Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm, Minamata.

SyllabusNode.title: Ancient India & Indus Valley Civilization
SyllabusNode.description: Harappan sites (Dholavira, Lothal, Rakhigarhi), Town planning, Vedic Age (Rigvedic vs Later Vedic), Buddhism & Jainism (Councils, Sects, Philosophy), Mauryan Empire, Ashokan Edicts.

SyllabusNode.title: Medieval India & Dynasties
SyllabusNode.description: Delhi Sultanate (Iltutmish, Alauddin Khalji, Muhammad bin Tughlaq), Mughal Administration (Mansabdari, Zabt system), Vijayanagara Empire (Krishnadevaraya), Bhakti & Sufi movements.

SyllabusNode.title: Modern Indian History & Freedom Struggle
SyllabusNode.description: British Expansion (Plassey, Buxar, Subsidiary Alliance, Doctrine of Lapse), Revolt of 1857, Socio-Religious Reform Movements, INC Foundation (1885), Partition of Bengal & Swadeshi (1905).

SyllabusNode.title: Gandhian Era & National Movement (1915–1947)
SyllabusNode.description: Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad, Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience (Salt Satyagraha), Quit India Movement (1942), INA & Subhas Chandra Bose, Cabinet Mission 1946, Mountbatten Plan.

SyllabusNode.title: Indian Art, Architecture & Literature
SyllabusNode.description: Temple Architecture (Nagara, Dravida, Vesara), Cave Architecture (Ajanta, Ellora, Bhimbetka), Classical Dances (8 Sangeet Natak Akademi forms), Folk Dances, Indian Music (Hindustani vs Carnatic).

SyllabusNode.title: Space Technology & Astronomical Missions
SyllabusNode.description: ISRO launch vehicles (PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, SSLV), Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1, Gaganyaan, NISAR, James Webb Space Telescope, Gravitational Waves (LIGO-India).

SyllabusNode.title: Biotechnology, Genetics & Health
SyllabusNode.description: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, mRNA vaccines, CAR-T cell therapy, Stem cells, Rare diseases, Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), One Health concept, Sickle Cell Anaemia elimination.

SyllabusNode.title: Defense Technology & Nuclear Program
SyllabusNode.description: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (Prithvi, Agni series, BrahMos, Akash), Aircraft Carriers (INS Vikrant), Ballistic vs Cruise missiles, Nuclear triad, S-400 system.

SyllabusNode.title: Information Technology, AI & Emerging Tech
SyllabusNode.description: Artificial Intelligence, Large Language Models, Quantum Computing (National Quantum Mission), Semiconductor manufacturing (India Semiconductor Mission), Web3, 5G/6G.

SyllabusNode.title: Reading Comprehension & Critical Reasoning
SyllabusNode.description: Identifying Central Idea, Author Assumptions, Inferences, Logical Corollaries, Strengths/Weaknesses of arguments.

SyllabusNode.title: Quantitative Aptitude & Number Systems
SyllabusNode.description: Number properties, Remainder theorem, Divisibility rules, Permutations & Combinations, Probability, Percentages, Profit & Loss, Time & Work, Speed Time Distance.

SyllabusNode.title: Logical & Analytical Reasoning
SyllabusNode.description: Syllogisms, Seating arrangement, Blood relations, Direction sense, Puzzles, Coding-decoding, Data Sufficiency, Series completion.

SyllabusNode.title: Indian Culture, Architecture & Literature from Ancient to Modern Times
SyllabusNode.description: Salient aspects of art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times, regional styles, patronage, revival.

SyllabusNode.title: Modern Indian History & Post-Independence Consolidation
SyllabusNode.description: Significant events, personalities, issues during freedom struggle; reorganization of states, tribal integration, linguistic disputes.

SyllabusNode.title: Indian Society: Diversity, Women, Globalization & Urbanization
SyllabusNode.description: Role of women and women’s organizations, population and associated issues, poverty, developmental issues, urbanization problems, effects of globalization, secularism, regionalism, communalism.

SyllabusNode.title: World Physical Geography & Resource Distribution
SyllabusNode.description: Distribution of key natural resources across the world including South Asia, factors responsible for the location of primary, secondary, and tertiary sector industries.

SyllabusNode.title: Indian Constitution: Comparison, Federalism & Separation of Powers
SyllabusNode.description: Comparison of the Indian constitutional scheme with other countries; separation of powers between organs, dispute redressal mechanisms, federal structure challenges.

SyllabusNode.title: Governance, Transparency, Citizen Charters & E-Governance
SyllabusNode.description: Aspects of governance, transparency and accountability, e-governance applications, models, successes, limitations, citizen charters, role of civil services in a democracy.

SyllabusNode.title: Social Justice, Welfare Schemes & Health/Education
SyllabusNode.description: Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections by the Centre and States, performance of mechanisms, laws, institutions; issues relating to development of Health, Education, Human Resources.

SyllabusNode.title: International Relations: Bilateral, Regional & Global Groupings
SyllabusNode.description: India and its neighbourhood-relations, bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India and/or affecting India’s interests, effect of policies of developed and developing countries.

SyllabusNode.title: Indian Economy & Issues Relating to Planning, Mobilization & Growth
SyllabusNode.description: Issues relating to planning, mobilization of resources, growth, development and employment, inclusive growth and issues arising from it, government budgeting.

SyllabusNode.title: Agriculture: Cropping Patterns, Irrigation, PDS, E-Technology & Subsidies
SyllabusNode.description: Major crops cropping patterns in various parts of the country, different types of irrigation, storage, transport and marketing of agricultural produce, direct and indirect farm subsidies, food security.

SyllabusNode.title: Science & Technology: Indigenization & Intellectual Property Rights
SyllabusNode.description: Achievements of Indians in science & technology; indigenization of technology, developments in IT, Space, Computers, Robotics, Nanotechnology, Bio-technology, IPR issues.

SyllabusNode.title: Disaster Management, Environmental Degradation & Climate Change
SyllabusNode.description: Disaster and disaster management, environmental impact assessment (EIA), conservation, environmental pollution and degradation.

SyllabusNode.title: Internal Security Challenges: Terrorism, Extremism, Cyber Security & Borders
SyllabusNode.description: Linkages between development and spread of extremism, role of external state and non-state actors in creating challenges to internal security, money-laundering, security challenges in border areas.

SyllabusNode.title: Ethics and Human Interface: Essence, Determinants & Consequences
SyllabusNode.description: Essence, determinants and consequences of Ethics in human actions; dimensions of ethics; ethics in private and public relationships; human values – lessons from the lives of great leaders.

SyllabusNode.title: Attitude, Emotional Intelligence & Moral Thinkers
SyllabusNode.description: Content, structure, function of attitude; its influence and relation with thought and behaviour; moral and political attitudes; emotional intelligence concepts and application; contributions of moral thinkers.

SyllabusNode.title: Public/Civil Service Values and Ethics in Public Administration
SyllabusNode.description: Status and problems; ethical concerns and dilemmas in government and private institutions; laws, rules, regulations and conscience as sources of ethical guidance; accountability and ethical governance.

SyllabusNode.title: Probity in Governance & Ethics Case Studies Methodology
SyllabusNode.description: Concept of public service; philosophical basis of governance and probity; information sharing and transparency in government, Right to Information, Codes of Ethics, Citizen’s Charters; Case Studies on above issues.

SyllabusNode.title: Philosophical & Abstract Themes (Section A & B)
SyllabusNode.description: Multi-dimensional thematic brainstorming, epistemological perspectives, ethical dilemmas, balance of arguments, quotes, and synthesis.

SyllabusNode.title: Socio-Economic, Technology & Governance Themes
SyllabusNode.description: Structured essays using the PESTLE framework (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental, Ethical), national priorities, and visionary conclusions.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Functions of a Constitution, Authority of Constituent Assembly, Objective Resolution, Institutional Arrangements, Borrowed Features.
NCERTChapter.summary: Explains why societies need a constitution to coordinate rules, limit government power, and express collective aspirations.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Bill of Rights, Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35), Preventive Detention, Writs (Article 32), DPSP (Part IV), Relation between FR and DPSP.
NCERTChapter.summary: Comprehensive analysis of constitutional rights, writ remedies under Articles 32 and 226, and the Kesavananda Bharati basic structure balance.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: First Past the Post (FPTP) system, Proportional Representation (PR), Delimitation Commission, Election Commission of India (Art 324), Electoral Reforms.
NCERTChapter.summary: Contrasts FPTP and PR systems, explains why India chose FPTP for Lok Sabha and Assemblies, and outlines powers of the Election Commission.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Parliamentary vs Presidential executive, President of India (election, veto, discretionary powers), Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, Permanent Executive (Civil Services).
NCERTChapter.summary: Deconstructs the parliamentary executive in India, constitutional position of President vs Prime Minister, and role of Bureaucracy.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Bicameralism, Rajya Sabha special powers, Legislative procedure, Money Bill vs Ordinary Bill, Parliamentary Committees, Anti-Defection (10th Schedule).
NCERTChapter.summary: Analyzes why Parliament is needed, how laws are enacted, role of Parliamentary Standing Committees, and anti-defection provisions.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Independence of Judiciary, Appointment of Judges (Collegium System), Original, Appellate, Advisory Jurisdictions, Judicial Review, Public Interest Litigation (PIL).
NCERTChapter.summary: Examines constitutional safeguards for judicial independence, jurisdiction of Supreme Court, judicial activism, and PIL evolution.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Division of Powers (7th Schedule Union/State/Concurrent), Centre-State Relations, Governor’s Role, President’s Rule (Art 356), Interstate River Water Disputes.
NCERTChapter.summary: Studies the unitary tilt of Indian federalism, emergency powers, interstate council, and federal frictions.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, 11th and 12th Schedules, Gram Sabha, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission, PESA Act 1996.
NCERTChapter.summary: Traces the evolution of Panchayati Raj, 3-tier local governance structure, reservation for women, and financial devolution challenges.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Case studies of Belgium and Sri Lanka, Majoritarianism vs Accommodation, Horizontal and Vertical power sharing.
NCERTChapter.summary: Highlights the prudential and moral reasons for sharing power among legislature, executive, judiciary, and levels of government.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Coming together vs Holding together federations, Linguistic States, Language policy, Centre-State relations, Decentralization in India.
NCERTChapter.summary: Focuses on linguistic reorganization of states, 3-tier decentralization post-1992, and the coalition era of federalism.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Functions of political parties, Multi-party system, National vs State recognized parties criteria, Challenges facing political parties.
NCERTChapter.summary: Criteria by Election Commission for recognizing national and state parties, role of opposition, and internal democracy reforms.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Colonial exploitation, Land settlement systems (Zamindari, Ryotwari, Mahalwari), De-industrialization of handicrafts, Drain of Wealth theory.
NCERTChapter.summary: Detailed examination of stagnation in agricultural, industrial, and foreign trade sectors under colonial British rule.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Five Year Plans goals (Growth, Modernization, Self-reliance, Equity), Mahalanobis model, Land Reforms, Green Revolution, Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR 1956).
NCERTChapter.summary: Studies state-led industrialization, import substitution, public sector dominance, and agricultural transformation through Green Revolution.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: 1991 Balance of Payments crisis, Structural Adjustment Program, LPG reforms, Disinvestment, Financial sector reforms, WTO establishment.
NCERTChapter.summary: In-depth review of 1991 LPG reforms, industrial de-licensing, devaluation, capital account liberalization, and post-reform growth.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Sources of human capital (Education, Health, On-the-job training, Migration, Information), Human capital vs Human development, Education cess.
NCERTChapter.summary: Explains how investment in health and education enhances productivity and economic growth in developing countries.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Rural credit (NABARD, Regional Rural Banks, SHG-Bank Linkage), Agricultural marketing, Organic farming, Diversification into livestock and fisheries.
NCERTChapter.summary: Critical challenges in rural credit, role of micro-finance, agricultural supply chain bottlenecks, and sustainable agriculture.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: ICAR classification of soils: Alluvial, Black (Regur), Red & Yellow, Laterite, Arid, Saline, Peaty, Forest soils. Soil erosion and conservation.
NCERTChapter.summary: Soil profile, geographical distribution across India, mineral composition, fertility, self-ploughing capacity of black soil, and leaching in laterites.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Functions of environment, Carrying capacity, Absorptive capacity, Land degradation, Global warming, Brundtland Commission, Sustainable development strategies.
NCERTChapter.summary: Connects environmental degradation, ozone depletion, and climate change to economic growth, focusing on non-conventional energy and bio-composting.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Circular Flow of Income, GDP, GNP, NDP, NNP at Factor Cost vs Market Price, Real vs Nominal GDP, GDP Deflator, Limitations of GDP as welfare measure.
NCERTChapter.summary: Fundamental macroeconomic identities, three methods of calculating national income (Value Added, Income, Expenditure), and externalities.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Functions of Money, Demand for Money, High Powered Money (M0), Money Multiplier, Commercial banks credit creation, RBI monetary policy instruments (CRR, SLR, Repo).
NCERTChapter.summary: Analyzes monetary aggregates (M1, M2, M3, M4), liquidity management, credit creation by banking system, and Central Bank quantitative/qualitative controls.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Revenue Receipts vs Capital Receipts, Revenue Expenditure vs Capital Expenditure, Fiscal Deficit, Revenue Deficit, Primary Deficit, Deficit financing.
NCERTChapter.summary: Components of Union Budget, distinction between capital and revenue budgets, fiscal deficit implications, and debt sustainability.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Balance of Payments (Current Account & Capital Account), Balance of Trade, Autonomous vs Accommodating transactions, Fixed vs Floating Exchange Rates, NEER & REER.
NCERTChapter.summary: Deconstructs external trade transactions, exchange rate determination, depreciation vs devaluation, and capital account convertibility.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: The Origin and Evolution of the Earth
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Nebular hypothesis, Big Bang theory, Evolution of lithosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere.
NCERTChapter.summary: The geological evolution of planet earth, differentiation of layers, and origin of oceans and life.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Sources of earth interior info (Direct vs Indirect), Earthquake waves (P and S waves, Shadow zones), Crust, Mantle, Core (Nife), Discontinuities (Mohorovicic, Gutenberg).
NCERTChapter.summary: Primary physical evidence from seismology, shadow zones of P and S waves, asthenosphere, and density structure of earth interior.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Continental Drift Theory (Alfred Wegener), Conventional Current Theory, Seafloor Spreading (Harry Hess), Plate Tectonics, Plate Boundaries (Divergent, Convergent, Transform).
NCERTChapter.summary: Evidence for continental drift, mid-oceanic ridges, paleomagnetism, and plate tectonic boundaries (Ring of Fire).

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Atmospheric gases, Troposphere, Stratosphere (Ozone layer), Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Ionosphere, Lapse rate.
NCERTChapter.summary: Thermal structure of atmosphere, vertical temperature distribution, importance of stratospheric ozone, and radio transmission layers.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Insolation, Factors controlling temperature, Heat budget of the earth, Terrestrial radiation, Temperature inversion.
NCERTChapter.summary: Earth heat budget balance, albedo of surfaces, greenhouse warming mechanism, and winter temperature inversion in valleys.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Coriolis force, Planetary winds (Trades, Westerlies, Polar Easterlies), Hadley, Ferrel and Polar cells, Jet Streams, Tropical vs Extra-tropical Cyclones.
NCERTChapter.summary: Tri-cellular atmospheric circulation, pressure belts, monsoon mechanism, and genesis of tropical cyclones over warm oceans (>27°C).

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Waves, Tides (Spring and Neap tides, Lunar attraction), Ocean Currents (Warm currents vs Cold currents, Gulf Stream, Kuroshio, California, Humboldt, Benguela).
NCERTChapter.summary: Ocean water circulation patterns, Coriolis effect on gyres, fishing grounds formed by mixing of warm and cold currents, and tidal energy.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Latitudinal and longitudinal extent, Indian Standard Meridian (82°30’ E), Territorial waters, Frontiers with neighbouring countries.
NCERTChapter.summary: Geographical position of India, standard time calculation, strategic significance in the Indian Ocean, and international land boundaries.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Peninsular Block, Himalayas and extra-peninsular mountains, Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain, Coastal Plains (Western vs Eastern), Island groups (Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep).
NCERTChapter.summary: Detailed morphological classification of Himalayas (Greater, Lesser, Shiwaliks), Bhabar, Tarai, Bhangar, Khadar plains, and Western vs Eastern Ghats.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Himalayan drainage (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra), Peninsular drainage (Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Narmada, Tapti), Evolution of river systems, River regimes.
NCERTChapter.summary: Exhaustive comparative study of Himalayan antecedent rivers vs Peninsular consequent rivers, drainage patterns (Dendritic, Trellis, Radial).

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Factors determining climate of India, Mechanism of Indian Monsoon (Thermal concept, Dynamic concept, Jet streams, Tibetan heating, Somali jet, ENSO, IOD).
NCERTChapter.summary: Complete scientific treatment of monsoon onset, break in monsoon, retreat of monsoon, El Nino Southern Oscillation, and Indian Ocean Dipole.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Early vs Mature Harappan, Town planning, Citadel and Lower town, Drainage system, Craft production (Chanhudaro), Trade contacts (Mesopotamia / Dilmun), Seals, Script, Decline.
NCERTChapter.summary: Archaeological insights into Indus Valley Civilization, Dholavira water reservoirs, Lothal dockyard, and social differences.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies (c. 600 BCE - 600 CE)
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Sixteen Mahajanapadas, Rise of Magadha, Mauryan Empire, Ashokan Edicts (Dhamma, script deciphment by James Prinsep), Land grants and agrarian expansion, Guptas administration.
NCERTChapter.summary: Epigraphic and numismatic evidence for early historic state formation, trade guilds (shrenis), and administration under Mauryas and Guptas.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments (c. 600 BCE - 600 CE)
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Sanchi Stupa conservation, Teachings of the Buddha (Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path), Sangha, Hinayana vs Mahayana, Jainism (Tirthankaras, Mahavira teachings, Ahimsa), Early temple architecture.
NCERTChapter.summary: Philosophical revolt against Vedic ritualism, architecture of Buddhist stupas (harmika, anda, chhatri), and sculpture preservation.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Permanent Settlement in Bengal (1793, Sunset Law, Jotedars), Santhal Revolt (Damin-i-Koh, Sidhu & Kanhu), Deccan Riots Commission (1875, Cotton boom, Moneylenders).
NCERTChapter.summary: Agrarian distress under East India Company revenue systems, tribal resistance in Rajmahal hills, and peasant rebellion in the Deccan.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Rebels and the Raj: The 1857 Revolt and Its Representations
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Outbreak in Meerut, Delhi, Awadh annexation (Lord Dalhousie, Nawab Wajid Ali Shah), Leaders (Bahadur Shah Zafar, Nana Sahib, Rani Lakshmibai, Kunwar Singh), Proclamations, British suppression.
NCERTChapter.summary: Causes, spread, and visual representations of the 1857 Revolt, mutiny of sepoys, peasant participation, and post-1857 structural changes.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement: Civil Disobedience and Beyond
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: South African experiments, Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22), Chauri Chaura, Salt March (Dandi 1930), Civil Disobedience, Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Round Table Conferences, Quit India Movement (1942).
NCERTChapter.summary: Evolution of mass nationalism under Gandhi, satyagraha technique, social base of Congress, and peasant/women involvement.

NCERTChapter.chapterTitle: Framing the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era
NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Constituent Assembly debates (1946-49), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Jawaharlal Nehru (Objective Resolution), K.M. Munshi, Debate on Fundamental Rights, Language debate, Separate electorates controversy.
NCERTChapter.summary: Critical ideological debates in Constituent Assembly regarding federalism, minority safeguards, official language, and social justice.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Abiotic factors (Temperature, Water, Light, Soil), Adaptations, Population attributes, Population growth models (Exponential vs Logistic growth, Carrying capacity), Species interactions (Mutualism, Commensalism, Parasitism, Amensalism, Competition - Gause principle).
NCERTChapter.summary: Ecological hierarchy, physiological adaptations in desert/aquatic organisms, logistic growth curves, and interspecific population interactions.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Ecosystem structure and function, Productivity (GPP vs NPP), Decomposition, Energy flow (10% law), Ecological Pyramids (Number, Biomass, Energy - always upright), Ecological Succession (Hydrarch vs Xerarch, Climax community), Nutrient cycling (Carbon and Phosphorus cycles).
NCERTChapter.summary: Trophic structure of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, upright vs inverted biomass pyramids, and pioneer to climax community succession.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Levels of biodiversity (Genetic, Species, Ecological), Latitudinal gradients, Species-Area relationship (Alexander von Humboldt), Importance of biodiversity (Rivet Popper hypothesis), Causes of biodiversity loss (The Evil Quartet: Habitat loss, Over-exploitation, Alien species invasion, Co-extinctions), In-situ vs Ex-situ conservation.
NCERTChapter.summary: Global biodiversity patterns, reasons for tropical diversity, extinction threats, sacred groves, biosphere reserves, national parks, and international biodiversity treaties.

NCERTChapter.keyTopics: Air pollution (Electrostatic precipitator, Catalytic converter, Air Act 1981), Water pollution (BOD, Eutrophication, Biomagnification of DDT/Mercury), Solid waste management, Radioactive wastes, Greenhouse effect and global warming, Ozone depletion in stratosphere (Dobson units, Montreal Protocol), Deforestation (Chipko movement, JFM).
NCERTChapter.summary: Pollution control technologies, biochemical oxygen demand in polluted water bodies, chlorofluorocarbons mechanism in ozone hole creation, and joint forest management.

Explanation.summary: The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156(1)). There is no constitutional provision for removal by the State Legislative Assembly.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Under Article 155, the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. Under Article 156(1), the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President. The State Legislative Assembly has no role in the appointment or removal/impeachment of the Governor. Under Article 154(1), the executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Option C asserts a legislative impeachment procedure akin to the President or Judges. The Constitution does not grant State Assemblies any mechanism to remove a Governor.
Explanation.sourceCitation: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (7th Ed.), Chapter 30: Governor
Explanation.relatedConcept: Constitutional Position and Removal of Governor

Explanation.summary: Statement 1 is correct. The MPC is a 6-member body (not 12) chaired by the RBI Governor (not the Finance Minister).
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Under Section 45ZB of the amended RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee consists of 6 members: the RBI Governor (ex-officio Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer, and three external members appointed by the Central Government for a tenure of four years.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Statements 2 and 3 are standard factual traps. The Finance Minister does not chair the MPC; the RBI Governor presides over it.
Explanation.sourceCitation: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Chapter on Monetary Management & RBI Act Section 45ZB
Explanation.relatedConcept: Monetary Policy Framework Agreement & MPC Composition

Explanation.summary: Kanha National Park (Madhya Pradesh) is the sole surviving natural habitat of the hard-ground Barasingha (Rucervus duvaucelii branderi).
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The hard-ground barasingha is the state animal of Madhya Pradesh and was brought back from the brink of extinction through dedicated conservation in Kanha Tiger Reserve. Kanha's mascot, 'Bhoorsingh the Barasingha', was created in celebration of this successful conservation program.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Associate hard-ground swamp deer directly with Central Indian sal and bamboo grasslands of Kanha.
Explanation.sourceCitation: Shankar IAS Environment, Protected Area Network & Wildlife Conservation

Explanation.summary: Both statements are reversed and incorrect. In Mitakshara, sons acquire ownership by birth; Dayabhaga applies primarily in Bengal and Assam where ownership is acquired only after the father's demise.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Under the Mitakshara school (Vijnaneshwara), a son acquires by birth an interest in the ancestral property. Under Dayabhaga (Jimutavahana), there is no birthright; sons acquire property only upon the father's death. Furthermore, Mitakshara prevailed across India except Bengal and Assam, whereas Dayabhaga prevailed in Bengal/Assam.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: UPSC frequently tests classical legal treatises by inverting their key attributes: Mitakshara = birthright; Dayabhaga = demise of father.
Explanation.sourceCitation: A.L. Basham, The Wonder That Was India, Social and Legal Institutions
Explanation.relatedConcept: Hindu Jurisprudence & Inheritance Schools (Mitakshara vs Dayabhaga)

Explanation.summary: Both statements are correct. Positive IOD involves warmer sea surface temperatures in the western Indian Ocean and often boosts the Indian Southwest monsoon.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is an ocean-atmosphere phenomenon in the equatorial Indian Ocean. During a Positive IOD, the western Indian Ocean (near the African coast) becomes warmer than average, leading to greater convection and moisture transport towards the Indian subcontinent, frequently mitigating the negative impacts of El Niño.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Statement 1 is the textbook definition of IOD. Statement 2 represents the established positive correlation with monsoon precipitation.
Explanation.sourceCitation: NCERT Class XI Physical Geography, Atmospheric Circulation and Weather Systems

Explanation.summary: Lagrange points are positions in space where gravitational forces of two large bodies balance the centripetal force needed to move with them, enabling an uninterrupted view of the Sun.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Aditya-L1 was placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrangian point L1, located about 1.5 million km from Earth. A satellite in halo orbit around L1 has the major advantage of continuously viewing the Sun without any occultation/eclipses.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: L1 for Aditya-L1 is a Sun-Earth system point, not Earth-Moon (Option A is eliminated). Option B accurately defines the orbital equilibrium.
Explanation.sourceCitation: ISRO Mission Profile — Aditya-L1 Solar Observatory & Science Notes

Explanation.summary: Dividing by 100 requires factors of 100 (which is 4 × 25). The expression contains 85 (5 × 17), 95 (5 × 19), and 96 (4 × 24). Thus 5 × 5 × 4 = 100 is an exact factor, giving remainder 0.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Notice the prime factors in the numerator: 85 = 5 × 17, 95 = 5 × 19, and 96 = 4 × 24. Multiplying the factors: 5 × 5 × 4 = 100. Since 100 is a complete factor of the numerator, the entire product is an exact multiple of 100. Therefore, the remainder upon division by 100 is 0.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Check if the product is divisible by 25 (ends in two 5s) and 4 (ends in a multiple of 4). Both exist: 85 & 95 contribute 25; 96 contributes 4. Remainder is guaranteed to be 0.
Explanation.sourceCitation: CSAT Quantitative Aptitude, Number Theory & Factorization

Explanation.summary: Knowing Saturday is studied and Sunday is not, with a rule of max 2 non-study days, leaves multiple valid study patterns for Thursday. Thus S1 and S2 together are not sufficient.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Let the days be Monday through Sunday. S2 tells us: Sat = Study, Sun = No Study. S1 tells us: at most 2 consecutive No-Study days. This means Monday could be No Study (making Sun-Mon two days) or Study. Tracing backwards to Thursday, Thursday could be Study or No Study without violating the constraint.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Construct counter-examples: Pattern A: (Thu=Study, Fri=Study, Sat=Study, Sun=No) and Pattern B: (Thu=No, Fri=Study, Sat=Study, Sun=No). Both satisfy S1 and S2, but give opposite answers for Thursday.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC CSAT Analytical Reasoning, Data Sufficiency Principles

Explanation.summary: The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 was enacted to overcome adverse judicial rulings (such as Kameshwar Singh, Romesh Thappar, and Champakam Dorairajan).
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The 1st Amendment Act, 1951 introduced Article 31A, 31B, and the Ninth Schedule to immunize agrarian land reforms against judicial review under Articles 14, 19, and 31. It also amended Article 19(2) adding reasonable restrictions on freedom of speech and added Article 15(4) to enable special provisions for advancement of socially and educationally backward classes.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Notice the historical context: 1951 land reform court battles occurred immediately post-independence. The 1st Amendment introduced the Ninth Schedule specifically for this reason.
Explanation.sourceCitation: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter on Constitutional Amendments & Granville Austin
Explanation.relatedConcept: First Constitutional Amendment & Ninth Schedule Genesis

Explanation.summary: Pioneered by Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, this method creates mini urban forests with native species planted densely, growing 10x faster.
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The Miyawaki method involves planting two to four types of indigenous trees within every square metre. The saplings receive direct sunlight only from the top, causing them to grow upwards rather than outwards. The forest becomes 30 times denser and grows 10 times faster than conventional monoculture plantations.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Miyawaki = Japanese urban micro-forestry. Widely featured in Indian urban municipal initiatives (Chennai, Delhi, Mumbai).
Explanation.sourceCitation: Down to Earth & Ministry of Environment Forest Reports

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option D
Explanation.detailedExplanation: A private member bill is any bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a Minister. Both elected and nominated non-ministers can introduce them. Around 14 private member bills have been enacted into law since independence (the last in 1970). Both statements are false.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2017)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option B
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Under MMDR Amendment Act 2015, District Mineral Foundations are non-profit bodies created in mining districts to work for the interest and benefit of persons and areas affected by mining-related operations through Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana (PMKKKY).
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2016)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option C
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Bank Rate is the standard rate under Section 49 of the RBI Act at which RBI buys or rediscounts bills of exchange (long-term lending without collateral). Reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI absorbs liquidity from commercial banks against government securities.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2015)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option C
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The Buddha was born in Shakya republic, attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Magadha), and preached extensively in Kosala (Shravasti) and Magadha (Rajgriha). Avanti and Gandhara were distant northwest and western kingdoms where Buddha never physically traveled in his lifetime.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2014)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option A
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Voting in public elections is a statutory/legal right (Representation of the People Act 1951), but is NOT listed in the 11 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A (Swaran Singh Committee had recommended making voting a duty, but it was not accepted).
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2013)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option B
Explanation.detailedExplanation: CPCB is a statutory organisation constituted in September 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, not an executive order. Therefore Statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 correctly outlines NGT judicial mandate vs CPCB pollution control functions.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2012)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option A
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Bluetooth is a WPAN (Wireless Personal Area Network) technology operating at 2.4 GHz for short ranges. Wi-Fi is a WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network) technology operating across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands. Statement 2 reverses the two network classifications.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2011)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option A
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 along with Article 31B to protect agrarian land reform laws from judicial review.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2024)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option A
Explanation.detailedExplanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30’ N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Answer Key (2023)

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option C
Explanation.detailedExplanation: Under Article 76, the President appoints a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney-General for India. Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India and can take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote.
Explanation.eliminationTechnique: Elimination technique: Verify whether Statement 1 overstates the statutory origin. Statement 2 provides the core conceptual attribute (Kalyana mandapas with intricately carved monolithic pillars), guiding resolution to Option A.
Explanation.sourceCitation: UPSC Official Final Master Key (2024)
Explanation.explanationEn: Under Article 76, the President appoints a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney-General for India. Under Article 88, the Attorney General has the right of audience in all courts in India and can take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote.
Explanation.explanationHi: अनुच्छेद 76 के तहत राष्ट्रपति सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश बनने की योग्यता रखने वाले व्यक्ति को भारत का महान्यायवादी नियुक्त करते हैं। अनुच्छेद 88 के तहत उन्हें संसद के दोनों सदनों की कार्यवाही में भाग लेने और बोलने का अधिकार है, परंतु मतदान का अधिकार नहीं है। दोनों कथन सत्य हैं।

Explanation.summary: Official UPSC answer: Option D
Explanation.detailedExplanation: All three are included in UNESCO WNBR: Nilgiri (2000, India first), Sunderbans (2001), and Similipal (2009). Currently 12 of India 18 biosphere reserves are in the World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Supreme Court Constitution Bench Rules on Electoral Autonomy and Article 324 Powers
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: A Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court reiterates that plenary powers under Article 324 must operate in harmony with Parliamentary statutes and democratic transparency.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: A five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court clarified the scope of the Election Commission of India's (ECI) constitutional prerogatives under Article 324. The Court affirmed that while Article 324 confers reservoir powers where statutes are silent, it cannot operate as an unbridled legislative authority overriding the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and 1951.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Constitutional status of ECI, Article 324, 325, 326, Delimitation Act, and appointment procedure under the Chief Election Commissioner Act.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper II: Appointment of constitutional authorities, separation of powers, electoral reforms, and maintaining institutional integrity.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: PRS Legislative Research & Supreme Court Judgments
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Article 324, Plenary Powers, Representation of the People Act, Model Code of Conduct, Delimitation
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Article 324 vests superintendence of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures in the ECI. Panchayats/Municipalities are conducted by State Election Commissions (Article 243K).
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Free and fair elections form an unalterable part of the Basic Structure doctrine (Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain, 1975).

CurrentAffairsStory.title: MoEFCC Designates Two New Wetland Complexes as Ramsar Sites in Peninsular India
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: India's Ramsar network expands to 85 sites with the designation of vital bird sanctuaries and estuarine ecosystems in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has announced the accession of two critical ecological habitats to the List of Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention. These ecosystems act as major wintering feeding stops along the Central Asian Flyway (CAF) for migratory waterbirds such as the bar-headed goose and greater flamingo.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Ramsar Convention criteria, Montreux Record, ecological criteria for wetland protection, and location mapping of wetlands.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper III: Biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation through coastal wetlands, ecosystem services, and community-led conservation (Amrit Dharohar).
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Ramsar Sites, Montreux Record, Central Asian Flyway, Amrit Dharohar, Wetland Rules 2017
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Ramsar Convention signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran. Sundarbans is the largest Ramsar site in India; Renuka in Himachal Pradesh is the smallest.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Wetlands act as natural sponges against coastal storm surges and flood inundation while filtering urban wastewater without capital-intensive infrastructure.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: India and ASEAN Conclude Review Round of the Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA)
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: India and ASEAN negotiators advance discussions to modernize rules of origin and rectify trade asymmetries in the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) signed in 2009.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: Senior trade officials from India and the 10 member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) convened to review the bilateral trade agreement. India has sought stricter Rules of Origin (ROO) to curb circumvention of goods originating from third countries, enhanced tariff concessions for Indian agricultural and engineering exports, and streamlined non-tariff measures (SPS and TBT) to address India's expanding bilateral trade deficit.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: ASEAN member nations, Rules of Origin, Non-Tariff Barriers (SPS/TBT), Act East Policy, and key multilateral economic groupings in the Indo-Pacific.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper II: India's neighborhood and Act East diplomacy, bilateral trade balances, regional economic integration, and supply chain diversification.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: AITIGA, Rules of Origin, Non-Tariff Barriers, Act East Policy, Circumvention
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: ASEAN was founded in 1967 with the Bangkok Declaration. The 10 members are Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: India's trade deficit with ASEAN grew from $5 billion in 2010 to over $40 billion, necessitating value-chain upgrading and strict origin certifications.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Cabinet Approves Coastal Logistics Hubs Under National Green Hydrogen Mission
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Union Cabinet sanctions port-based Green Hydrogen and Ammonia export hubs at Deendayal (Kandla), Paradip, and Tuticorin under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Union Cabinet has sanctioned infrastructure outlays under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) to establish three mega coastal hubs at Kandla, Paradip, and V.O. Chidambaranar Port (Tuticorin). The hubs will integrate renewable power generation, electrolyzers, high-pressure desalination, and dedicated export jetties for green ammonia.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Electrolysis technology, differentiation between Grey, Blue, and Green Hydrogen, SIGHT scheme incentives, and port export logistics.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper III: Energy independence, decarbonizing hard-to-abate industrial sectors (fertilizers, refineries, steel), and global green energy exports.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Green Hydrogen, Electrolyzer, SIGHT Scheme, Blue vs Green Hydrogen, Ammonia Cracking
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Green hydrogen is produced by water electrolysis using renewable electricity (solar/wind). Grey hydrogen utilizes steam methane reforming without carbon capture.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Decarbonizing steel and cement requires high enthalpy heat where electrification is unviable; green hydrogen serves as a direct chemical reducing agent.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: ISRO Completes Qualification of Semi-Cryogenic Pre-Burner Ignition Engine for LVM3
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: ISRO successfully validates the 2000 kN semi-cryogenic engine at Mahendragiri, enabling higher payload capacity for Gaganyaan and deep space missions.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has marked a major milestone in propulsion technology with the successful hot-testing of the Semi-Cryogenic Pre-Burner Ignition system at the ISRO Propulsion Complex (IPRC) in Mahendragiri. The semi-cryogenic engine utilizes refined kerosene (Isrosene) as propellant and liquid oxygen (LOX) as oxidizer, replacing liquid core stages in LVM3 launch vehicles.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Propulsion comparison (Cryogenic vs Semi-cryogenic), Isrosene fuel characteristics, specific impulse, and LVM3 payload enhancements.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper III: Indigenization of technology, space exploration milestones, heavy-lift launch vehicle capabilities, and commercial satellite launch economics.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Semi-Cryogenic Engine, Isrosene, Liquid Oxygen (LOX), Specific Impulse, LVM3, Gaganyaan
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Cryogenic engines use liquid hydrogen (fuel, -253°C) and liquid oxygen (oxidizer, -183°C). Semi-cryogenic engines replace liquid hydrogen with refined kerosene, which is denser and storable at ambient temperatures.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Semi-cryogenic stages increase payload delivery to Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO) from 4 tonnes to 6 tonnes, saving multi-million-dollar foreign launch fees.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: RBI Framework on Central Bank Digital Currency (e-Rupee) Interoperability
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Reserve Bank of India expands retail e-Rupee pilot by integrating QR code interoperability with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) enabled complete interoperability between the Digital Rupee (e-Rupee CBDC) and the UPI ecosystem. The sovereign digital currency functions as legal tender recorded on a distributed ledger, eliminating settlement risk without requiring an underlying commercial bank intermediary.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Distinction between CBDC and cryptocurrency, legal tender status, Coinage Act, and RBI balance sheet liabilities.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 3: Financial inclusion, monetary sovereignty, cross-border remittance efficiency, and de-dollarization.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: CBDC, e-Rupee, UPI Interoperability, Distributed Ledger, Legal Tender, Fiat Currency
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: CBDC is a sovereign currency in digital form appearing as a direct liability on the central bank balance sheet, unlike commercial bank deposits.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Reduces physical currency management costs (over Rs. 4,000 crores annually) and provides programmable welfare disbursals.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: RBI Releases Framework for Climate-Related Financial Disclosures by Regulated Entities
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued guidelines mandating commercial banks and top NBFCs to disclose climate-related financial risks and carbon exposure under TCFD pillars.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) published guidelines on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures for Regulated Entities (REs). Anchored upon four core pillars: Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics & Targets, the framework strengthens Indian banking resilience against physical and transition risks.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Understand Green Finance, TCFD framework, differences between physical risk vs. transition risk, and RBI regulatory mandate.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper III: Sustainable economic development, mobilization of resources, green banking, and climate adaptation finance.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Reserve Bank of India (Official Press Release)
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Green Financing, TCFD Pillars, Physical Risk, Transition Risk, Regulated Entities (REs)
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: TCFD was established by the Financial Stability Board (FSB) in 2015. RBI joined the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) in April 2021.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Mobilizing climate finance requires an estimated $2.5 trillion by 2030 for India's NDC targets. Mandatory disclosures mitigate greenwashing.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Great Nicobar Holistic Island Development & Shompen Tribe Habitat Conservation
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Environmental and anthropological review of the Rs. 72,000 crore mega-transshipment port and greenfield airport project in Great Nicobar.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change reviewed mitigation protocols for the Great Nicobar Holistic Development Project. The island hosts the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve and Campbell Bay National Park, which are crucial habitats for the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) Shompen and Nicobarese, alongside nesting sites of the Leatherback Sea Turtle.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: PVTGs criteria, Great Nicobar geography, Ten Degree Channel, Campbell Bay National Park, Galathea Bay.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 1 & 3: Strategic Indo-Pacific maritime chokepoints vs. indigenous rights, biodiversity loss, and ecological fragility in tectonic zones.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Shompen, PVTG, Galathea Bay, Leatherback Turtle, Malacca Strait, Campbell Bay
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Galathea Bay is the world's most significant nesting site for the giant Leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea).
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Strategic imperative: Located within 40 nautical miles of the international Malacca Strait shipping lane.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Aditya-L1 Solar Mission Reaches Halo Orbit around Lagrange Point 1
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: ISRO successfully injects India's first dedicated solar observatory into its halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 point, 1.5 million km from Earth.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: ISRO's Aditya-L1 spacecraft achieved halo orbit insertion around the first Lagrange point (L1). The position allows an unobstructed view of the Sun without occultation or eclipses. The payload suite includes VELC (Visible Emission Line Coronagraph) and SUIT (Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope) to analyze coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and solar flares.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Lagrange points physics, solar corona temperature anomaly, coronal mass ejections, geomagnetic storms.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 3: Space technology achievements, space weather monitoring, and protection of critical satellite constellations.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Aditya-L1, Lagrange Point, VELC, Corona, Halo Orbit, Solar Flares, CME
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: At Lagrange point L1, gravitational pull of two large masses equals the centripetal force required for a small object to orbit with them.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Protects critical telecommunications, GPS satellites, and electrical power grids from Carrington-like geomagnetic disturbances.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Delimitation Commission & Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Constitutional Mandates
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Analytical review of the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act reserving one-third seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 inserts Article 330A, 332A, and 239AA(2)(b) reserving 33% seats for women. The operationalization is linked to the completion of the first decennial census after enactment followed by a nationwide delimitation exercise under Article 82.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Article 82, Delimitation Commission Act, 84th & 87th Constitutional Amendments, Article 330A, Article 334A sunset clause.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2: Women empowerment in political leadership, federal representation disputes between southern and northern states.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Ministry of Law & Justice / Gazette of India
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Article 330A, Delimitation, 106th Amendment, Article 82, Federalism, Census
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Reservation is enacted for a period of 15 years from commencement with provision for rotation of seats.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Addresses descriptive vs substantive political representation; resolves southern states' demographic penalty concerns.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) & GRAP Stage IV Regulations
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Implementation of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) Stage IV under the statutory powers of the CAQM Act in the National Capital Region.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 'Severe+' threshold (AQI > 450) triggered Stage IV of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021 empowers the commission to ban non-essential diesel medium and heavy goods vehicles, stop construction, and mandate hybrid schooling.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: CAQM statutory powers, EPCA replacement, AQI pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb), stubble burning penal provisions.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 3: Environmental governance, cooperative federalism across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi, agricultural bio-decomposers.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Commission for Air Quality Management / PIB
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: CAQM, GRAP Stage IV, AQI, Stubble Burning, Air Act 1981, Bio-decomposer
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: AQI measures 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Statutory evolution: Replaced Supreme Court-mandated EPCA with a permanent statutory authority with penal powers up to Rs. 1 crore and 5 years imprisonment.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: PM-JANMAN: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan Tribal Mission
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Comprehensive socio-economic saturation mission covering 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups across 18 states and UTs.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Union Cabinet sanctioned Rs. 24,104 crore for PM-JANMAN targeting 75 PVTG communities living in 22,000 remote habitations. The mission converges 11 critical interventions across 9 line ministries including pucca housing under PMAY-G, tap water connectivity under Jal Jeevan Mission, and off-grid solar electrification.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Dhebar Commission (1973), criteria for identifying PVTGs (pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, declining population, economic backwardness).
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2: Vulnerable sections welfare, decentralized tribal governance, FRA 2006 compliance, and tribal health disparity.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: PM-JANMAN, PVTG, Dhebar Commission, Forest Rights Act 2006, PMAY-G
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: There are 75 identified PVTGs in India, with Odisha having the highest number of PVTG communities (13).
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Shifts tribal administration from generic schematic funding to target-habitation household saturation.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 & Data Protection Board Structure
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Statutory framework governing consent-based processing of digital personal data and the establishment of the Data Protection Board of India.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The DPDP Act 2023 creates a comprehensive regulatory regime for processing digital personal data. It enshrines seven principles including lawful purpose, data minimization, and accuracy. It introduces the concepts of 'Data Fiduciary' and 'Data Principal', and creates an adjudicatory Data Protection Board with monetary penalties up to Rs. 250 crore.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Puttaswamy privacy judgment (2017), Article 21, Data Principal vs Data Fiduciary, Consent Manager, Cross-border data transfer rules.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2 & 3: Right to privacy vs state exemptions (national security), surveillance concerns, ease of doing business for startups.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology / Gazette
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: DPDP Act 2023, Puttaswamy Doctrine, Data Fiduciary, Data Principal, Article 21
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Applies exclusively to digital personal data; does not apply to non-personal data or data processed by individuals for personal/domestic purposes.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Balances fundamental right to informational privacy under Article 21 with innovation in the trillion-dollar digital economy.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) Strategic Implications
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Multilateral infrastructure initiative connecting India to Europe via ship-to-rail transit through the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Israel.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: Announced on the sidelines of the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Summit, IMEC comprises two corridors: the East corridor linking India to the Arabian Gulf, and the Northern corridor linking the Arabian Gulf to Europe. It incorporates railway networks, electricity cables, clean hydrogen export pipelines, and high-speed data cables.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Port geography (Mundra, JNPT, Jebel Ali, Haifa, Piraeus), Strait of Hormuz bypass, clean energy connectivity.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2: Geopolitics of global trade corridors, alternative to China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), Middle East de-escalation.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Ministry of External Affairs / G20 India
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: IMEC, G20 New Delhi, Haifa Port, BRI Counter, Clean Hydrogen, Multimodal Transit
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Expected to increase transit speed between India and Europe by 40% and reduce logistics costs by 30%.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Reconfigures Eurasian trade architecture, institutionalizing India's role as a reliable global supply-chain anchor.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Inter-State River Water Disputes Act & Cauvery Water Management Authority Orders
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Constitutional mechanisms governing inter-state river water sharing under Article 262 and distress-sharing formulas during monsoon deficits.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and Regulation Committee issued binding orders directing Karnataka to release designated cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu. Deficit rainfall in the catchment basin reignited debates over the need for a scientific distress-sharing formula under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: Article 262, Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956, Supreme Court jurisdiction bar under Article 262(2), Cauvery river tributaries (Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathi, Kabini, Bhavani, Noyyal, Amaravati).
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2: Cooperative federalism, institutional efficacy of water tribunals, climate change impact on river basins.
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Article 262, CWMA, Cauvery Basin, Distress Formula, Tribunal Award
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Under Article 262(2), Parliament may by law provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction over interstate river disputes.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Highlights systemic delay in tribunal awards (average 15-20 years) and the necessity of real-time telemetry river monitoring.

CurrentAffairsStory.title: Supreme Court Guidelines on Governor's Assent under Article 200
CurrentAffairsStory.summary: Three-judge bench rules that Governors cannot sit indefinitely on bills passed by State Legislatures, reiterating the constitutional mandate of 'as soon as possible'.
CurrentAffairsStory.content: The Supreme Court of India delivered a landmark judgment interpreting Article 200 of the Constitution. The Court clarified that the phrase 'as soon as possible' conveys constitutional urgency. When a Governor withholds assent, the bill must be returned to the legislature with a message. If passed again, the Governor must grant assent, underscoring federal harmony and parliamentary democracy.
CurrentAffairsStory.importancePrelims: High yield for Article 200, Article 201 (Presidential reservation), and Sarkaria / Punchhi Commission recommendations on Governors.
CurrentAffairsStory.importanceMains: GS Paper 2: Federalism, Governor's discretionary powers, and institutional frictions between elected state executives and gubernatorial office.
CurrentAffairsStory.sourceName: Supreme Court of India / The Hindu
CurrentAffairsStory.termsList: Article 200, Pocket Veto, Sarkaria Commission, Federalism, Basic Structure
CurrentAffairsStory.prelimsFodder: Governor has 4 options under Article 200: Assent, Withhold, Return for reconsideration (non-money bills), or Reserve for President.
CurrentAffairsStory.mainsFodder: Reiterates Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab doctrine: Governor must act on aid and advice of Council of Ministers except in rare constitutional exceptions.
